newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS GIANT SLALOM, SEIZINGER SECOND.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS GIANT SLALOM, SEIZINGER SECOND.

text.p: Italy's Deborah Compagnoni underlined her giant slalom dominance by winning the World Cup Finals race on Saturday to end her season with four victories in a row.

Compagnoni, second to Katja Seizinger of Germany after the first run, was brilliant on the top of the second run as she powered her way through the 48-gate course for a combined time of two minutes, 11.45 seconds.
Seizinger took second place in 2:11.83, a result that lifted her past Austrian Anita Wachter into second place in the season giant slalom standings behind Compagnoni.
Wachter, who held a nine-point edge over Seizinger in the standings entering the race, finished ninth in 2:13.13.

Third place went to Swiss Karin Roten in 2:12.07, 0.44 of a second ahead of Italian speed specialist Isolde Kostner. It was the first visit to the World Cup podium this season for Roten, who took giant slalom silver at the world championships.
Overall champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden finished fifth ahead of France's Sophie Lefranc.
"I really wanted to win the last race of the season," said Compagnoni, who also triumphed with two gold medals at the world championships at Sestriere.
Noting Kostner's surprisingly strong result, Compagnoni added:."It was a big day for Italy."

The result provided another layer of silver to Seizinger's season. Seizinger, last season's overall champion, had already captured second place in the overall and in the downhill and Super-G disciplines.
